title: As a founder, the core transaction this service exists for (form, register, apply, file, or pay) can be completed online, per the service's own published pages
As a founder, I can start the core online flow without creating an account first — the service's published pages document a keyless or file-number entry path
As a founder, a paper, fax, or mail fallback rail is published with the exact addresses, numbers, and forms, so the task can still be completed when the online flow is unavailable
As a founder, any operating-hours window, per-day limit, or session timeout on the online flow is published up front, before I start
As a developer, the service documents a public API for its data — published endpoints, a key-issuance path, and stated rate limits on its own pages
As a developer, a machine-readable specification for the service's machine channel is published — an OpenAPI spec, XML schemas, or a data dictionary
As a developer, the service publishes bulk public-data downloads or extracts (datasets, registry extracts, wage or case statistics) that need no scraping

As a legal-ops lead, a documented system-to-system channel exists for software to transact with the service (system accounts, transmitter programs, batch providers), with the enrollment path published
As a legal-ops lead, the service documents a sanctioned third-party rail — designees, authorized providers, registered agents, or representatives — through which a provider can act for my company
As a legal-ops lead, exactly what a third party may and may not do on my behalf is published — the authorization forms, the roles, and which signatures stay personal
As a founder, the service publishes exactly which account, credential, and identity-proofing steps stand between me and filing — stated before I start, not discovered mid-flow
As an AI-native founder, the published sign-in path is credential MFA an authorized human can complete remotely — not biometric liveness, an in-person visit, or a PIN by physical mail
As a founder, I can look up the status of my filing, application, or case from the service's public pages
As a founder, current processing times for my transaction type are published by the service itself
As a founder, the exact statutory fees for my transaction are published on the service's own pages — amounts, not a contact form
As a founder, the filing deadlines and the penalty and interest schedule for missing them are published with exact figures
As a founder, the service publishes plain-language, step-by-step guidance for my task — explainers a non-lawyer can follow, not just statute text and form numbers
As a founder, the forms themselves and their instructions are downloadable from the service's site without an account

As an AI-native founder, the service's published guidance pages are reachable by a keyless agent with a standard identified user agent — no bot wall, JS-only shell, or CAPTCHA in front of the public reading surface
As an AI-native founder, the service publishes a real robots.txt, so an agent can know what it may read before fetching anything
